title: Which AI is most accurate at researching a person? What RECON found
summary: Which AI is most accurate at researching a person? On RECON, the benchmark we built, Sixtyfour XHigh has the highest weighted accuracy: 70.6 percent.
body_markdown:
On RECON, a benchmark of 514 verified facts about 140 real people, Sixtyfour XHigh has the highest weighted accuracy, 70.6 percent, from 434 correct answers, 71 wrong and 9 missing. The strongest system from another company is Parallel Ultra 2x at 41.1 percent, and the strongest model called through an AI lab's own API is Grok 4.20 multi-agent from xAI at 36.2 percent. Sixtyfour built RECON and five of the 23 configurations are ours; the benchmark page names HUD under "Externally validated by", and HUD ran every configuration with our dataset and public harness.


RECON did not test the ChatGPT app. It ran OpenAI's models through OpenAI's API with web search, and the strongest, GPT-6 Astra, scored 25.1 percent weighted accuracy. It was right on 90.6 percent of the answers it gave, the highest precision of any system tested, and it left 355 of the 514 fields blank and found 28.0 percent of the facts, so on RECON its answers were mostly right and had many gaps. The ChatGPT app may use different tools and settings.


Yes. Sixtyfour researches a person from a name and a few identifying details and returns the fields you ask for, each with a confidence score from 0 to 100, a justification and the pages it was read on. On RECON, its XHigh configuration has the highest weighted accuracy of the 23 tested, and XHigh is the default engine in Atlas, its deep investigation product. Anything it could not establish is reported as open, and a person on your team decides.


Weighted accuracy is the number of correct answers minus the number of wrong answers, divided by all the fields requested. A correct answer earns a point, a wrong answer loses a point and a blank earns nothing, so an extra answer raises the score only when it is more likely right than wrong. RECON's public repository calls the same measure net accuracy.


Precision counts only the fields a system answers. GPT-6 Astra answered 159 of the 514 fields and got 144 right, which is 90.6 percent, while Sixtyfour XHigh answered 505 and got 434 right, which is 85.9 percent. XHigh found three times as many facts and gave 56 more wrong answers, so it is higher on weighted accuracy and recall while GPT-6 Astra is higher on precision.


Sixtyfour built RECON and its dataset and offers five of the 23 configurations evaluated, so read it as our benchmark. The benchmark page names HUD under "Externally validated by", and HUD ran every configuration between 8 September and 6 October 2026 with the dataset and our public harness. The harness and scoring code are on GitHub, the dataset is available on request because it contains personal information, and each score comes from a single run.


A GPT-4.1 mini judge marks each field correct, wrong or missing, ignoring differences of format, and it agreed with human review on 98.5 percent of a 200-field sample. A field counts as missing when the system returns nothing for it. Every reference answer was verified against a primary source with an unambiguous link to the person.
